Before you begin 06 / 06

A few
useful details.

What kind of geometry does it create?

Project Damage generates geometry for wear, fractures, cuts and structural details. Individual effects have their own mesh requirements: some need a solid volume, while sheet effects work on thin surfaces. Check the matching guide before building the final mesh.

Can I keep editing the original?

Yes. The generated result stays linked to an editable source while you work. You can switch between the original and the damage result. Apply All bakes the final stack and keeps a hidden editable source.

Is every effect a physics simulation?

Effects are primarily artist-directed geometry tools. Supported physics workflows can fill the damaged region, fracture it and simulate the resulting pieces. Timber and metal presets describe a visual treatment; they do not model engineering material strength.

How do I install it?

Use the add-on ZIP that matches your Blender version and platform. In Blender, go to Edit → Preferences → Add-ons → Install from Disk. Enable project_damage, then open its tab in the 3D Viewport sidebar. The previews on this page come from the Blender 5.2 build.

What about materials and documentation?

The add-on has a local user manual with installation instructions and individual effect guides. An optional Project Damage CC0 Materials pack connects separately through the add-on's Preferences. Damage materials and structural materials can be adjusted in the relevant effect settings.

Will the result match the previews?

Your source mesh, real-world scale, thickness and quality settings influence the result. Start with moderate detail, use Draft while placing damage and inspect the full-quality mesh before applying it.
